headline: Town officials examined major FY28 operating and capital shortfalls while the Select Board sponsored zoning changes to expand senior housing.
synopsis: Southborough boards focused heavily on FY28 budget planning, assessing departmental service cuts and staffing reductions across public safety and schools under level funding. The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee confronted a one million dollar capital request gap and evaluated options to adjust the town bonding threshold. The Select Board voted to advance and sponsor a Town Meeting zoning amendment lifting the townwide cap on over-55 senior housing. In other matters, town officials initiated plans to review scenic road tree removal restrictions, and the Board of Health tracked upcoming expirations in regional public health grant funding.

highlights.title: FY28 departmental operating budgets and potential override
highlights.why: Departments submitted level-service and level-funded budgets, warning that level funding would eliminate police and dispatch positions, reduce fire shift minimums, and cut 15 school staff members.

highlights.title: Senior housing zoning amendment sponsorship
highlights.why: The Select Board voted to refer to the Planning Board and sponsor an article to lift Southborough's 7 percent cap on senior housing while requiring 12.5 percent affordability.

highlights.title: FY28 capital budget strategy and funding gap
highlights.why: Town capital requests reached 2.2 million dollars against a 1.2 million dollar tax-funded placeholder, prompting discussion about lowering the bonding threshold to borrow for larger projects.

highlights.title: K-8 Public Schools capital improvement requests
highlights.why: School officials presented 710,000 dollars in capital requests across three schools, prioritizing Woodward School concrete stair replacement and Finn School fence repairs.

highlights.title: Public shade tree policy and scenic road review
highlights.why: The Select Board agreed to schedule a public hearing to consider rescinding or amending local shade tree rules that delay the removal of hazardous trees along designated scenic roads.

highlights.title: State public health blueprint and grant funding
highlights.why: Health officials reported on state commission updates and began tracking state advocacy as the regional Public Health Excellence grant expires at the end of FY27.
